newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent dips to new low as gasoline sheds gains.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent dips to new low as gasoline sheds gains.

text.p: IPE Brent made a fresh session low on Wednesday afternoon as early gains made by NYMEX gasoline were quickly retraced, traders said.

July Brent was trading steady at $19.22 a barrel at 1511 GMT, having hit a session low of $19.18 moments earlier. NYMEX unleaded gasoline, the market leader with the U.S. gasoline season now officially underway, bounced early on but then slipped.
"Technically it was expected, a spike followed by a sell-off," a trader said.
Brent was lodged in a narrow 16-cent range with trade cautious after Tuesday's losses and ahead of the release of U.S. stocks data due after the market's close.
June gas oil was trading $1.25 higher at $173.25 a tonne.
"There's not a whole lot happening...It's the calm after the storm," said one dealer.
Heavy falls on Tuesday were attributed to investment funds liquidating long positions.
News that Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) has cancelled two cargoes of Basrah Light crude earlier helped the market gain a few cents.

The two cargoes, both due to load in the next week before the six-month U.N. oil-for-food deal expires, were cancelled amid concerns that Iraq would overshoot its $2.14 billion revenue limit, a U.N. source said.
